analyses.what_happens: Step 1: i_rst_n_rd=i_rst_n_wr=i_rst_n_sw=1, i_rd_en=1, o_empty=1, o_sw_rst_busy=0. The i_clk_rd rising edge at step 2 samples these values, so the antecedent is true and the obligation is pending (nnc_fv_s_CHK_002=1 at steps 2-3). In the same step 2, i_rst_n_rd goes to 0. The asynchronous reset clears reg_underflow. At step 3, i_rst_n_rd goes back to 1 on a FALLING i_clk_rd edge (clk 1->0), so no rising edge ever samples it low. The next rising edge (step 4) samples step 3: i_rst_n_rd=1, so disable iff is not active, and o_underflow=0. The |=> consequent fails. The whole reset pulse lies between two sampled edges and is released off a rising edge.
analyses.spec_says: spec/AsyncGrayFIFO_Design_Specification.md:267 (RST-L, rule AF-6.2-03): "Asserted asynchronously, de-asserted synchronously to the clock of its domain, already synchronized outside the IP. It shall stay low for at least one clock edge of its domain so that the flops are reset". Spec :431 (AF-7.3-02): RST-RD "Deassertion: Controlled by the integrator, synchronous to i_clk_rd; Reset value: Pointers 0, empty 1, underflow 0". Spec :153 (REQ-RESET-001, AF-3-34) and :1454 (ASM-001, AF-20.1-01): the resets are already synchronized to their clocks. The CHK-002 contract text (contract.json:268) requires "i_rst_n_rd=1 at both" edges and does not mention a reset between them.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:150-155: reg_underflow has an asynchronous reset on negedge i_rst_n_rd and is otherwise <= i_rd_en & ~w_rd_blk & w_empty_n. :199: o_underflow = reg_underflow. The reset at step 2 clears it, as required by CHK-001/REQ-RESET-002. The RTL behaves correctly for the reset it was given.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_rd.sv:62-64: `@(posedge i_clk_rd) disable iff (!i_rst_n_rd) (i_rd_en && o_empty && i_rst_n_wr && i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy) |=> o_underflow`. The disable condition is effectively evaluated only at sampled i_clk_rd edges. A reset pulse that is asserted and released between two edges is invisible to the checker. nnc_env.sv:41-58 has no assumption about how the hardware resets are deasserted (ENV-01..ENV-04 only).

candidates.evidence_for: The trace releases i_rst_n_rd at step 3, which is a falling edge of i_clk_rd. This breaks the obligation that the reset is deasserted synchronously to the clock of its domain and stays low for at least one clock edge (spec:267 AF-6.2-03, spec:431 AF-7.3-02, spec:153 AF-3-34, spec:1454 AF-20.1-01). nnc_env.sv does not model this obligation. Under it, the release can only happen in the step of a rising i_clk_rd edge, so that edge samples i_rst_n_rd=0 and disable iff kills the pending obligation. The CEX disappears.
candidates.evidence_against: If the designer wanted the checker to tolerate any asynchronous reset waveform, the checker could instead be made robust. The spec, however, explicitly forbids this waveform.

candidates.evidence_for: The checker samples i_rst_n_rd only at edges. The spec allows an asynchronous assertion at any time (spec:436 AF-7.3-07), and the property does not account for a reset that occurs strictly between edge n and edge n+1.
candidates.evidence_against: A reset that is both asserted and released between two rising edges is illegal per spec:267. With legal resets, the sampled disable iff is enough.

candidates.evidence_for: o_underflow=0 at edge n+1 after a non-blocked read while empty at edge n.
candidates.evidence_against: The pulse was cleared by an asynchronous hardware reset, which the spec requires (REQ-RESET-002, CHK-001). The RTL logic at rd.sv:154 produces the pulse correctly when no reset occurs.

analyses.options: E: add to nnc_env.sv an assumption for rule AF-6.2-03 / AF-7.3-02 / AF-3-34. Under the global/formal clock, i_rst_n_rd may rise only in the step where i_clk_rd rises, after having been low at a sampled edge (e.g. `always @($global_clock) if ($rose(i_rst_n_rd)) assume($rose(i_clk_rd));`). Add the same for i_rst_n_wr with i_clk_wr (AF-7.3-01). B (alternative, only if the designer wants robustness beyond the spec): add a helper flag that is set asynchronously by negedge i_rst_n_rd and cleared at the next i_clk_rd edge, and use it in the disable condition. No RTL change is indicated.

analyses.what_happens: A write is accepted at the i_clk_wr edge of step 2 (step 1: i_wr_en=1, both resets 1, i_rst_n_sw=1, o_full=0), so wbin becomes 1. At step 4, i_rst_n_wr is asserted ALONE: the write pointer goes back to 0 while the read domain stays out of reset. i_rst_n_wr is released at step 5, on a falling i_clk_wr edge. The read synchronizer has already caught Gray value 1, so o_empty=0 from step 5. At the read edge of step 7 (step 6: i_rd_en=1, o_empty=0) a read of this 'phantom' word is accepted: rbin=rgray=1. The synchronized write pointer becomes 0 (from the write reset), so w_occ = 0-1 = 15 (4-bit). o_empty stays 0, because rgray != wgray_s. i_empty_thr changes while a domain is in reset (15, then 8). At the read edge of step 9, which samples step 8 (i_empty_thr=8, o_empty_thr=0), clause (b) 'i_empty_thr >= DEPTH -> o_empty_thr=1' fails.
analyses.spec_says: Spec :1099 ERR-003 (AF-12-07): "Reset asserted in one domain only, after the FIFO was used | FIFO state inconsistent; not detected | None | Reset both domains | Integrator responsibility (ASM-005)". Spec :1461 ASM-005 (AF-20.1-05): "No FIFO operation (write or read) starts before both domains have left reset. Consequence, not a requirement: if one domain is reset alone after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent and the IP does not detect it." Spec :424: "If only one domain is reset after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent. The IP neither detects nor repairs this (ASM-005)." Spec :304: o_empty_thr = "Occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr (REQ-FUNC-010)". In addition, spec :267 / :430 (AF-6.2-03, AF-7.3-01): i_rst_n_wr is deasserted synchronously to i_clk_wr, and the trace breaks this at step 5.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:112: w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin (LPARA_PTR_W=4 bits, modular). :118: o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr). :97 and :117: o_empty = w_rd_blk | (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s). After the lone write reset (wr.sv:141-154 resets wbin/wgray), the read pointer is 1 ahead of the synchronized write pointer, so w_occ=15. 15 <= 8 is false, so o_empty_thr=0. This is the documented 'inconsistent state' of ERR-003. Away from that condition, the RTL computes the specified function.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_rd.sv:73-77 checks unconditionally at every i_clk_rd edge: (!o_empty || o_empty_thr) && (i_empty_thr < DEPTH || o_empty_thr) && (i_empty_thr != 0 || o_empty_thr == o_empty). It has no exclusion for the state after a one-domain reset following use. nnc_env.sv:51-58 (ENV-03/04, which already cite AF-12-07) only forces idle traffic while a reset is low. They do not forbid traffic after a lone reset until the other domain has also been reset.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure needs a one-domain hardware reset after the FIFO was used (write at step 2, lone i_rst_n_wr at step 4), followed by a read. ERR-003 (spec:1099, AF-12-07) classifies this as an error whose recovery is 'Reset both domains' and whose handling is 'Integrator responsibility'. The trace also releases i_rst_n_wr at step 5 on a falling i_clk_wr edge and both resets at step 1 with no clock edge, which breaks AF-6.2-03 / AF-7.3-01 / AF-7.3-02.
candidates.evidence_against: ASM-005 (spec:1461) says the inconsistency is a 'Consequence, not a requirement', and DEC-009 / AF-7.2-11 make the resets independent. So whether the environment is obliged to avoid a lone reset is ambiguous. Even with synchronous deassertion added, a lone-reset variant of this trace would very likely still fail, so the synchronous-deassertion assumption alone is not enough.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says that after a lone reset the state is 'inconsistent; not detected' (spec:424, :1099), so it defines no flag values there. A checker that demands threshold consistency at every edge, with no gating, claims more than the spec. The checker could track 'lone reset after use' and suspend clause (b) until both domains have been reset.
candidates.evidence_against: ERR-003 puts the responsibility on the integrator, which is more naturally an environment assumption than a checker exception.

candidates.evidence_for: ASM-005 ('Consequence, not a requirement') and ERR-003 ('Integrator responsibility') pull in different directions. Is a lone reset after use a legal input with undefined outputs, or a forbidden input? The answer decides between E and B.
candidates.evidence_against: Both readings agree that the DUT is not required to keep the flags consistent here, so the RTL is not at fault either way.

candidates.evidence_for: o_empty_thr=0 with i_empty_thr=8=DEPTH looks impossible for a consistent occupancy.
candidates.evidence_against: The occupancy estimate of 15 comes only from the lone-domain reset. The spec explicitly says the IP neither detects nor repairs this (spec:424, :436, :1099).

analyses.options: E: add an environment assumption for ERR-003 / ASM-005 (AF-12-07, AF-20.1-05). Once a write or read has been accepted, if one domain's hardware reset is asserted, no i_wr_en / i_rd_en until the other domain's reset has also been asserted and both are released. Do not assume that the resets are asserted together (DEC-009 allows them to be independent). Also add the synchronous-deassertion assumption of AF-6.2-03 / AF-7.3-01 / AF-7.3-02 (see CHK-002). B (if the designer reads ASM-005 as 'legal but undefined'): add a checker-side 'consistent' flag that is cleared by a lone reset after use and set again when both domains have been reset, and gate CHK-003 with it. C: ask the requester to say whether a lone reset after use is a forbidden input or a legal input with undefined outputs. No RTL change is indicated.

analyses.what_happens: The i_clk_rd rising edge at step 2 samples step 1 (i_rd_en=1, o_empty=1, resets 1), so o_underflow=1 at step 2. The negedge at step 3 captures cap_underflow=1. In the same step 3, i_rst_n_rd=0 asynchronously clears o_underflow to 0. i_rst_n_rd is released at step 4 with no i_clk_rd edge (clk stays 0). The rising edge at step 5 samples step 4: i_rst_n_rd=1 (disable iff inactive), cap_v=1, o_underflow=0 != cap_underflow=1, so the check fails. o_rd_data changes only at the rising edge of step 2 and is not involved.

Spec :272 (PULSE): 'Output of a flop'. Spec :267 (RST-L, AF-6.2-03): 'Asserted asynchronously, de-asserted synchronously to the clock of its domain ... It shall stay low for at least one clock edge of its domain so that the flops are reset'. Spec :431 (AF-7.3-02): deassertion 'synchronous to i_clk_rd'.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:150-155: reg_underflow is asynchronously reset on negedge i_rst_n_rd. :199: o_underflow = reg_underflow. The change at step 3 is exactly an 'assertion of i_rst_n_rd', which the behaviour allows.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_rd.sv:42-53 captures the outputs at negedge i_clk_rd. :81-84 compares them at the next posedge, with disable iff (!i_rst_n_rd) evaluated at the sampled point only. A reset that is asserted and released between the negedge capture and the next posedge is not seen, so the allowed reset-induced change is flagged. nnc_env.sv has no reset-deassertion assumption.

candidates.evidence_for: i_rst_n_rd is low only during step 3 and released at step 4 without any i_clk_rd edge. No edge ever samples it low. This breaks AF-6.2-03 (spec:267: deassert synchronously, stay low for at least one edge) and AF-7.3-02 (spec:431). With a release allowed only at a rising i_clk_rd edge, the edge at which the reset is released samples i_rst_n_rd=0 and disables the check, so the CEX goes away.

candidates.evidence_for: The behaviour explicitly allows a change at an assertion of i_rst_n_rd, but the checker only excludes it through a sampled disable iff. Its helper logic (cap_* at negedge) does not record a reset assertion that happens between captures.
candidates.evidence_against: Under legal (synchronously released, at-least-one-edge) resets, the sampled disable iff always covers the reset. The gap only appears with an illegal reset waveform.

candidates.evidence_for: o_underflow changed without a rising i_clk_rd edge.
candidates.evidence_against: The change was caused by an asynchronous hardware reset assertion, which the contract allows and REQ-RESET-002 requires.

analyses.options: E: add the synchronous-deassertion / minimum-width assumption of AF-6.2-03 / AF-7.3-02 for i_rst_n_rd (rise only in a step where i_clk_rd rises), and the same for i_rst_n_wr / i_clk_wr (AF-7.3-01). B (optional hardening): add an asynchronously set 'rst_seen' flag (set on negedge i_rst_n_rd, cleared at the posedge) and exclude edges where it is set. No RTL change.

analyses.what_happens: i_rst_n_sw=0 throughout. The i_clk_wr rising edge at step 2 samples step 1 (i_rst_n_wr=1, o_sw_rst_busy=0, i_rst_n_sw=0), so the FSM leaves RUN. In the same step 2, i_rst_n_wr=0 asynchronously resets the FSM and the busy flop (busy=0). i_rst_n_wr is released at step 3, on a falling i_clk_wr edge. The rising edge at step 4 samples step 3: i_rst_n_wr=1, so not disabled. $past(i_rst_n_sw)=0 from step 1, so the checker expects busy=1, but busy=0. The failure comes from a reset pulse that no i_clk_wr edge sampled low.
analyses.spec_says: Spec :267 (AF-6.2-03): RST-L is 'de-asserted synchronously to the clock of its domain ... It shall stay low for at least one clock edge of its domain so that the flops are reset'. Spec :430 (AF-7.3-01): RST-WR 'Deassertion: Controlled by the integrator, synchronous to i_clk_wr'. Spec :436 (AF-7.3-07): the hardware resets act asynchronously on the FSMs at any time and have priority over the software reset. The contract (contract.json:383, CHK-007) requires o_sw_rst_busy=0 at the reset assertion.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:193-198 and :208-213: the FSM and reg_sw_rst_busy are asynchronously reset to RUN/0 on negedge i_rst_n_wr. :171-174: RUN goes to REQ when !i_rst_n_sw. :202: busy_nxt = (nxt != RUN). Without the reset pulse, busy would rise at edge 2. The reset correctly overrides it.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:101-103: `disable iff (!i_rst_n_wr) (!o_sw_rst_busy) |=> (o_sw_rst_busy == !$past(i_rst_n_sw))`. The reset is evaluated only at sampled i_clk_wr edges, so a reset asserted and released between edges n and n+1 is invisible. nnc_env.sv has no assumption on reset deassertion.

With the release allowed only in a step where i_clk_wr rises, the release edge samples i_rst_n_wr=0, disable iff cancels the pending obligation, and this CEX cannot occur.

candidates.evidence_against: With legal resets (low for at least one edge, synchronous release), the sampled check is exact.

candidates.evidence_for: The CHK-010 wording 'with i_rst_n_wr=1 at both' does not explicitly say 'and no reset in between'.
candidates.evidence_against: Spec:267 makes an in-between pulse illegal, so the wording is enough under the environment rules.

analyses.options: E: add to nnc_env.sv the reset-deassertion assumption for AF-6.2-03 / AF-7.3-01 (i_rst_n_wr may rise only in the step of a rising i_clk_wr edge, so it is low at at least one sampled edge), and the analogous one for i_rst_n_rd (AF-7.3-02). B (optional): add an async 'reset seen since last edge' flag to the disable condition. No RTL change.

analyses.what_happens: i_rst_n_sw=0 throughout. The i_clk_wr edge at step 2 samples step 1 (busy=0, i_rst_n_sw=0), so busy=1 at step 2. The edge at step 4 samples step 3 (busy=1), so the antecedent holds and the obligation is pending. In the same step 4, i_rst_n_wr=0 asynchronously clears the FSM and busy. i_rst_n_wr is released at step 5, on a falling i_clk_wr edge (clk 1->0), so no rising edge ever sees it low. The edge at step 6 samples step 5: i_rst_n_wr=1 (not disabled), busy=0, $past(hist_ok)=0 (i_rst_n_sw was never 1), so the consequent fails. Busy fell because of a hardware reset, not because of a handshake release.
analyses.spec_says: Spec :267 (AF-6.2-03): reset 'de-asserted synchronously to the clock of its domain ... shall stay low for at least one clock edge'. Spec :430 (AF-7.3-01): RST-WR deassertion synchronous to i_clk_wr. Spec :436 (AF-7.3-07) / REQ-SRST-015 (AF-3-58): hardware reset has priority and resets the FSM asynchronously at any time. contract.json:492 (CHK-011) requires 'i_rst_n_wr=1 throughout'.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:193-198 and :208-213: an asynchronous reset of the FSM and reg_sw_rst_busy on negedge i_rst_n_wr. :168-190: busy can otherwise fall only through HOLD to REL to RUN, which needs i_rst_n_sw=1 and the flush check. The fall here is the required hardware-reset priority.

The 'throughout' condition is approximated by sampled disable iff, so a reset that sits entirely between two edges is missed.

With the release allowed only at a rising i_clk_wr edge, the edge at which the reset is released samples i_rst_n_wr=0, disable iff fires, and the CEX disappears.

analyses.what_happens: The i_clk_wr edge at step 2 accepts a write (step 1: i_wr_en=1, both resets 1, i_rst_n_sw=1, o_full=0), so wbin becomes 1. At step 3, i_rst_n_wr is asserted ALONE (released synchronously at the rising edge of step 4): the write pointer goes back to 0. The read synchronizer has already captured wgray=1, so o_empty=0 at step 5. A read is accepted at the read edge of step 7 (step 6: i_rd_en=1, o_empty=0), so rbin=rgray=1 (a phantom word). At step 9, i_rst_n_rd is asserted ALONE: rgray goes back to 0. The write-side synchronizer passes rgray=1, then 0. At step 11: i_rst_n_wr=1, i_rst_n_sw=1, busy=0, w_rgray_s=1, wbin=0, so w_occ = 0-1 = 15. o_full=0 (not the full pattern) and o_full_thr = (15 >= 8) = 1. The edge at step 12 samples i_full_thr=8: clause (c) requires o_full_thr == (o_full && sw && !busy) = 0, so it fails. Any threshold from 9 to 15 would fail clause (b) instead, so the i_full_thr changes (which ENV-01 allows while a domain is in reset) are not the root cause.
analyses.spec_says: Spec :1099 ERR-003 (AF-12-07): 'Reset asserted in one domain only, after the FIFO was used | FIFO state inconsistent; not detected | None | Reset both domains | Integrator responsibility (ASM-005)'. Spec :1461 ASM-005 (AF-20.1-05): 'No FIFO operation (write or read) starts before both domains have left reset. Consequence, not a requirement: if one domain is reset alone after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent and the IP does not detect it.' Spec :424: 'The IP neither detects nor repairs this (ASM-005).' Spec :291: o_full_thr = 'Occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr (REQ-FUNC-010)'. Spec :418 (CDC-004): thresholds are 'written once before the FIFO is used and not changed while it is in use'.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:120: w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s (4-bit modular). :106: w_full_n = (reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ MSK). :125-126: o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n; o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr==0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr). The lone resets of each domain (wr.sv:141-154, rd.sv:133-146) leave the read pointer 'ahead' of the write pointer, so occupancy is 15. This is the inconsistent state described by ERR-003. For consistent pointers (occupancy 0..8) the logic matches REQ-FUNC-010.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:123-130 checks clauses (a)-(d) at every i_clk_wr edge with i_rst_n_wr=1. There is no exclusion after a one-domain reset following use. nnc_env.sv:51-58 (ENV-03/04, citing AF-12-07) forbid traffic only while a reset is low. They allow the read at step 7 after the lone write reset.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure needs two one-domain hardware resets after the FIFO was used (lone i_rst_n_wr at step 3, lone i_rst_n_rd at step 9) with a read in between. ERR-003 (spec:1099, AF-12-07) names this condition, prescribes 'Reset both domains' as recovery, and assigns it to the integrator. Unlike CHK-003, this trace releases i_rst_n_wr synchronously (step 4 is a rising i_clk_wr edge), so the lone-reset obligation is the essential missing assumption.
candidates.evidence_against: ASM-005 (spec:1461) calls the inconsistency a 'Consequence, not a requirement', and DEC-009 / AF-7.2-11 make the resets independent. This leaves room to read a lone reset as a legal input with undefined outputs rather than a forbidden input.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec defines no flag values in the inconsistent state (spec:424, :1099). A checker that requires threshold consistency there goes beyond the spec. It could suspend the check from a lone reset after use until both domains have been reset.
candidates.evidence_against: 'Integrator responsibility' points to an environment obligation rather than a checker exception.

candidates.evidence_for: ASM-005 ('not a requirement') and ERR-003 ('Integrator responsibility') disagree on whether a lone reset after use is forbidden or merely gives undefined outputs. The answer decides between E and B.
candidates.evidence_against: Both readings agree the RTL need not keep the flags consistent, so either fix is outside the RTL.

candidates.evidence_for: o_full_thr=1 while o_full=0 with i_full_thr=DEPTH is impossible for a consistent occupancy.
candidates.evidence_against: It comes only from the occupancy estimate of 15 caused by lone-domain resets, which the spec says the IP neither detects nor repairs.
